question:
A 45-year-old female presents for a follow-up appointment with an infectious disease specialist. The
patient has a history of HIV and has been intermittently compliant with antiretroviral therapy. She has
been staying in a shelter with several individuals who have active tuberculosis infection. Her most
recent CD4 count was 167/mm3. The patient undergoes a screening Mantoux skin test, which is
negative. However, there is strong suspicion for underlying anergy. Which of the following is the most
appropriate treatment regimen for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide,
and ethambutol (B) Isoniazid and rifapentine combination therapy (C) Rifampin and pyrazinamide dual
therapy (D) Moxifloxacin and ethambutol combination (E) Daptomycin monotherapy (F) Azithromycin
and ethambutol (G) Isoniazid monotherapy (H) Streptomycin monotherapy (I) Observation and close
monitoring only (J) Rifabutin monotherapy
 A. Rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol
B. Azithromycin and ethambutol
C. Daptomycin monotherapy
D. Rifampin and pyrazinamide dual therapy
E. Observation and close monitoring only
F. Isoniazid and rifapentine combination therapy
G. Moxifloxacin and ethambutol combination
H. Isoniazid monotherapy
I. Rifabutin monotherapy
J. Streptomycin monotherapy
